description.summary: workspaces, outputs, tiling and pictures of a taskbar's windows

protocol.description:
The window menu of paw's taskbar moves a window to another workspace or output, keeps it on every workspace, or takes it out of the tiling, and the taskbar shows a small picture of a window while the pointer rests on its button. The taskbar knows its windows as zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 objects, which have no requests for that and no name a compositor could be asked about elsewhere; this protocol names a window by such a handle.
It gives a client nothing a foreign-toplevel client cannot already do to the window (close it, minimize it, make it fullscreen) or an ext-foreign-toplevel-list client cannot already see of it (capture it through ext-foreign-toplevel-image-capture-source-v1), and the compositor offers it as it offers zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1.
From version 3 it also says which process made each window, for the taskbar to find the sound a window plays among the sound server's streams. A client outside a sandbox can list the user's processes already; what this adds is which window is whose.
From version 4 the taskbar can peek at a window while the pointer rests on its picture, as Windows does: the other windows fade to show that one alone, wherever it is. This shows a window on the screen for a moment, as the picture shows it already, and changes nothing about it. Version 4 also gives each window's number, by which paw's control socket names windows, so that the shell finds the window its window switcher lists.
From version 5 it gives the icon a window supplies itself, through xdg-toplevel-icon-v1 or an X11 window's _NET_WM_ICON, for the taskbar to show a window whose application it cannot find among the desktop entries and icon themes, as a game run through Wine often is. A window supplies its icon for taskbars to show, as it does its title.
From version 6 it says whether a window is kept above the others, and keeps one above or lets it go back among them, for the window menu's Keep Above Others: what the compositor's toggle_above action does to the focused window.

interface.name: paw_window_control_v1

description.summary: controls windows named by their taskbar handles

interface.description: A global for getting the paw_window_v1 of a window, from the zwlr_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 the client holds for it.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: destroy the window control

request.description: The paw_window_v1 objects made through it keep working.

request.name: get_window

description.summary: the window a taskbar handle stands for

request.description: Creates a paw_window_v1 for the window `handle` stands for, which sends the window's state at once (output, workspace, state, from version 3 pid, from version 4 id, from version 5 its icon, then done; from version 6 the state says whether it is kept above) and again whenever it changes. A handle whose window is gone (one the client was sent closed for) gives an inert object, which sends nothing and whose requests do nothing.

interface.name: paw_window_v1

description.summary: one window's workspace, output and tiling

interface.description:
Where a window is and how it is placed, and requests that move it. It becomes inert when the window's taskbar handle is sent closed; the client then destroys it.
None of the requests focuses or raises the window. While the session is locked they do nothing.

entry.name: sticky
entry.summary: shown on every workspace of its output

entry.name: floating
entry.summary: kept out of the tiling: floated by the user, sticky, or a dialog

entry.name: tiled
entry.summary: a tile of its output's tiling

entry.name: tiling
entry.summary: the workspace it is on tiles windows automatically

entry.name: above
entry.summary: kept above the other windows of its output

entry.name: invalid_size
entry.summary: get_scaled_capture_source was given a width or height of 0

description.summary: destroy the object

request.name: move_to_workspace

description.summary: move the window to a workspace of its output

request.description: Moves the window to workspace `number` (from 1) of the output it is on, as the move_to_workspace action does for the focused window: a sticky window stops being sticky, a tile joins the tiling there or floats where that workspace does not tile, and a focused window that leaves the workspace shown passes the focus on. A number past the configured workspaces does nothing.

request.name: move_to_output

description.summary: move the window to another output

request.description: Moves the window onto the workspace output `name` (its connector name, as the output event gives it) shows: a floating window keeps its place relative to the output's usable area, a maximized one is maximized there, and a tile joins the tiling there or floats where that does not tile. A sticky window stays sticky. An output that is not connected, or the one the window is on, does nothing.

request.name: set_sticky

description.summary: show the window on every workspace

request.description: As the toggle_sticky action: the window floats and shows on every workspace of its output. Does nothing while features.sticky is off.

request.name: unset_sticky

description.summary: show the window on one workspace again

request.description: The window stays on the workspace its output shows, and tiles again if it was a tile.

request.name: set_floating

description.summary: take the window out of the tiling

request.description: A tile floats where it was before it tiled; a floating window stays out of the tiling when its workspace starts tiling.

request.name: unset_floating

description.summary: let the window tile

request.description: The window joins the tiling of its workspace when that tiles; a sticky one stops being sticky to do so.

event.name: output

description.summary: the output the window is on

event.description: The connector name of the output the window belongs to, "" before it is placed on one. The output may be gone: a window keeps its output while it waits for it to return.

event.name: workspace

description.summary: the workspace the window is on

event.description: The workspace of its output the window is on, from 1. A sticky window's follows the one its output shows.

event.name: state

description.summary: how the window is placed

event.description: A bitfield of the state enum.

event.name: done

description.summary: the state is complete

event.description: Sent after the output, workspace, state, pid, id, icon and icon_image events that describe one state of the window, so that the client applies them together. Only what changed is sent before it.

request.name: get_capture_source

description.summary: a capture source for the window

request.description:
Creates an ext_image_capture_source_v1 for the window, the one ext_foreign_toplevel_image_capture_source_manager_v1.create_source gives for its ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1: the window's own surfaces at its logical size, without the compositor's frame or shadow and without what overlaps it, also while it is minimized or on a workspace not shown. The client captures it with ext-image-copy-capture-v1.
The source is inert (a session made from it is stopped at once) when the window is gone or the session is locked, and a session stops when the window closes. Unlike the other requests, this one is not ignored on an inert paw_window_v1: it gives an inert source.

request.name: get_scaled_capture_source

description.summary: a capture source for a small picture of the window

request.description:
Creates an ext_image_capture_source_v1 for what get_capture_source captures, the window's own surfaces, scaled down to fit within `width` by `height` buffer pixels and keeping its aspect ratio. It is never scaled up: a window that fits already is captured at its logical size, as get_capture_source gives it. A frame's size follows the window's, each new one sent as the session's buffer constraints. The compositor scales smoothly, each pixel of a frame standing for all those it covers, so that a frame can be shown at its size as it is. A session's first frame comes at once, and each one after it once the window has changed. A width or height of 0 is an invalid_size error.
Each request makes a source of its own. Like get_capture_source's, it is inert when the window is gone or the session is locked, also on an inert paw_window_v1, and a session stops when the window closes; it is inert too when the window has many such sources already.

arg.name: width
arg.summary: the widest a frame may be, in buffer pixels

arg.name: height
arg.summary: the tallest a frame may be, in buffer pixels

event.name: pid

description.summary: the process the window belongs to

event.description:
The process id of the client that made the window, as the compositor sees it: the Wayland client's peer credentials, or for an X11 window the process its X client reports. 0 when it is not known. A taskbar matches it with what else names processes, such as the sound server's streams; a process inside a sandbox with a process namespace of its own knows itself by another number.
Sent with the window's state before done, and again should it change.

request.name: set_peek

description.summary: show the window alone over the desktop

request.description:
Peeks at the window, as a taskbar does while the pointer rests on its picture: every other window fades as the peek action fades them, to show the desktop, and this one shows in its place on its output over all of them, at its own opacity, below the panels. A minimized window shows where it was, and one on a workspace its output does not show shows over the workspace that it does. Nothing about the window changes: it is not focused, raised in the stacking order, restored or moved to the workspace shown, and a window shown only for the peek takes no input.
One window is peeked at a time. Peeking at another, through this client or another, moves the peek over to it while the other windows stay faded; peeking at the window peeked at already does nothing. The peek ends, with a fade, with unset_peek, or when this object is destroyed (as it is when its client disconnects), the window closes or is focused, the session locks, or the peek action starts.

request.name: unset_peek

description.summary: end the peek at the window

request.description: Ends the peek set_peek started through this object: the other windows fade back, and the window goes back to how it was, fading out again if it was not shown. Does nothing when that peek has ended, or moved to another window, already.

event.name: id

description.summary: the window's number

event.description:
A number the compositor gives the window as it first appears, and gives no other window while it runs; it is never 0. paw's control socket names windows by it where a handle cannot name them, as the window switcher's lines do.
Sent once, with the window's first state before done.

event.name: icon

description.summary: the window's own icon changed

event.description:
The icon the window supplies itself changed: through xdg-toplevel-icon-v1 for a Wayland window, or _NET_WM_ICON for an X11 one. `name` is the icon theme name it gave (xdg_toplevel_icon_v1.set_name), or null when it gave none, as an X11 window never does. The client drops the icon it had from the window, and an icon_image event follows when the window gave pixels.
Sent with the window's state before done: with its first state when the window has an icon as the object is made, and again each time the icon changes. When the window drops its icon, `name` is null and no icon_image follows. A window that has never had an icon sends no icon event.

arg.name: name
arg.summary: an icon theme name, or null

event.name: icon_image

description.summary: the pixels of the window's own icon

event.description:
The pixels of the icon the icon event before it announced: `fd` is a file of width * height * 4 bytes, rows of `width` pixels from the top with no padding between them, in wl_shm's argb8888 format (each pixel a native-endian 32-bit 0xAARRGGBB with its colour premultiplied by its alpha). The client maps it read-only, or reads it, and closes the fd; the compositor does not change the file once it is sent.
Of the sizes the window gave, the compositor sends one: the largest that fits within 256 by 256 pixels, else the smallest of the larger ones.

request.name: set_above

description.summary: keep the window above the others

request.description: As the toggle_above action: the window stays over the floating windows and tiles of its output, under fullscreen windows, the panels and the overlays. The members of a window group are kept above together.

request.name: unset_above

description.summary: let the window go back among the others

request.description: The window goes back among the other windows, in front of them.
